scope: Two exposed scripts, same legitimate history access: complete history versus completed-turn window plus incremental summary. Wiring only, not efficacy or long-history scaling.
split: exposed development; one repeat per arm/case

arm_contracts.full_history: Unchanged complete actual occurred owner history plus current prefix; no summary or State controller calls. Common read_history available.
arm_contracts.window_summary: Most recent2 whole completed turns plus current full ReAct prefix, and a separately labeled incremental summary of earlier completed turns. At most one summary attempt per public message. Common read_history accesses original checkpoints; incomplete old turns remain labeled raw data.

shared.full_history_capacity: Existing HostCapacity on entire actual request, no extra full-history truncation limit.

history_contract: Runtime indexes only actually visited public turns/sessions under the current run/arm/user, with actual chronological public-turn ordering across sessions.
Read final assistant/tool-call/result objects from public checkpoints, not copied progress answer strings or evaluator logs; current tool loop prefix is not duplicated.
Past capacity-failed prefixes retain actual side effects/status and original messages; do not fabricate completion or ToolMessage to make a chain look complete.

Both arms share the same mechanical cursor/max_bytes read_history tool and whole-record page budget. It extends a new matched tool schema; original answer/calls envelope and native/business tool semantics remain.
Owner-scoped checkpoint gets/logical bytes/CPU/wall and actual model usage charged; no new database or second persistent body archive.

Known tombstone under current owner conservatively suppresses new history tools/projection for that owner, including assistant echoes; other owner unaffected. This is not physical erasure of historical evidence.
Original checkpoints/raw messages retained; projections affect only actual request copies. No use of other-arm history or future script messages.

hypotheses.H1: A compact rolling summary can preserve evicted constraints and actions while reducing later Host prompt tokens; complete raw history remains an available strong baseline.
hypotheses.H2: Summary omissions, key rewriting or extra control cost may outweigh any input reduction; on these short histories the entire raw context may be simpler and cheaper.

scoring: Original p1-rubric full12 messages per arm. Preserve exact item_key/destination/packing, real partial receipt/get found/same-id label recovery, other owner isolation, all failures and skipped messages. Mechanism audit uses actual HTTP/summary commits/delivery/real actions, not normal exit.
mechanism_checks: Full-history actual HTTP matches original owner checkpoints/current prefix; off-path remains unchanged.

Actual first summary receives only prior evicted complete turns; committed summary and cursor survive separate phase processes. Subsequent summaries include exactly newly evicted completed turns, without resummarizing current tools.
Summary source/HTTP/Store commit/next Host system delivery and exact retained recent turns are auditable. Count all summary/Host/native memory costs.
Both arms use identical common read_history description/schema and owner scope. Report if no natural tool invocation, truncation or tombstone case occurs.
Both partial actual existing reservation reads and label completions use original IDs, with no extra reservation; report exact wrong keys under original rubric.
order_rationale: New window_summary first on interleaved; reverse on partial. Historical history-wiring-r1 results remain preserved; these are new same-source matched runs, not publication reruns or replacements.
isolation: Fresh run/arm/user State+LangMem namespaces, world/checkpoint/journal; independent phase processes.
source_freeze: Formal prepare only after source and protocol publication; bind actualsource/input/config/dependencies and freeze through all four trajectories.
stop_rule: All semantic/capacity/optional-control failures retain full denominators; stop affected execution on infrastructure/uncaught faults and diagnose before remaining originally planned independent runs. No replay/replacement.
next_decision: Retain all4 planned trajectories/costs. Diagnose only concrete integration faults; no wording loop on old key misses. Then remaining R/U=A/ablation, lifecycle/native task/scale/model obligations, without claiming short-history compression or stable benefit.

source_checks.pytest_command: uv run --no-sync --group baseline-langmem pytest -q tests/unit/test_local_state_attention.py tests/unit/test_langmem_application.py tests/unit/test_langmem_foundation.py

build.package_contents: sdist CLI and wheel summary.py verified

summary_contract: Read only actual visited scoped checkpoints in chronological public-turn order; no private observer history, rubric, future task, or offline answer.
Only whole COMPLETED assistant/tool-balanced turns enter window and summary cursor. Actual incomplete prefixes and business journal observations remain explicitly labeled raw data.
Only newly evicted completed turns plus previously committed summary go to the short generic summarizer; no current task in this maintenance input.
Summary text and covered visited ordinal commit together to one existing owner-scoped Store key. Original checkpoints remain; no new database or archive body copy.
At most one summary attempt per public message, including process restart; no new eviction means zero model calls. All actual successful/failed calls count in the same continuous ledger.

Known optional model timeout/truncation/invalid response may fall back to full original history, without advancing cursor or displaying uncommitted summary. Real Store read/write failure remains an explicit infrastructure fault. Existing request capacity still applies.
Owner tombstones suppress previous summary and history access/projection conservatively. Other owners stay isolated; this is not physical erasure.
post_task_user_instruction: After this current window_summary slice and its4 pre-registered trajectories, pause the active Goal; write an overall report and publish to GitHub. Do not start subsequent R/U=A/native/model work.
